book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time

chapters.file: ch41 - Chapter 6 - Performing Bullshit and the Post-Sincere Condition.md
chapters.relation: Concluding an essay on personality disorders, this chapter argues that pathological personalities (the antisocial, borderline, dependent, paranoiac) are especially good bullshitters and that their bullshit and distorted perceptions are what wreck their social relationships, since good relationships thrive on truth as much as on truthfulness. Against Frankfurt's claim that bullshit is the greater enemy of truth because indulging it erodes attention to reality, the author counters that the bullshitter does track truth at some level; bullshit's distinctive danger is that, unlike lying, it can be unconscious, so the sting of conscience never checks the habit.

chapters.file: ch43 - Shitty Attitudes On the Use and Misuse of Bullshit in Life.md
chapters.relation: This mini-essay opens by parodying a puffing university mission statement, aspiring to be 'one of the world's best philosophy essays' in the UBC mold. It then sets the agenda: Frankfurt left unanswered why our attitude toward bullshit is generally more benign than our attitude toward lying, and never considered bullshit's rhetorical uses and misuses - the two gaps the rest of the essay fills.

chapters.file: ch44 - Bullshit as a Condition of Life.md
chapters.relation: Reworking Frankfurt's Fania Pascal anecdote (Wittgenstein's disgusted 'You don't know what a dog that has been run over feels like'), the chapter argues that the bullshit that earns the retort 'That's bullshit!' is speech whose truth is irrelevant and which aims to evoke a positive attitude toward the speaker - hypochondriac pain complaints, boilerplate about graduate training in grant proposals, praise of the Dean to pass a hiring motion. It separates this from bullshit-as-entertainment and from courtesy conventions like thanking the gift-giving aunt, concluding against Frankfurt that pretentiousness is constitutive of at least this central kind of bullshit.

chapters.file: ch45 - The World as Will to Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: This section answers Frankfurt's exercise about benignity: bullshit is 'dishonesty without tears' because whole genres - grant proposals, Fourth of July oratory, letters of reference - generically require performative values everyone knows count for nothing, like compulsory figures in figure skating. Rejecting free-riding as the origin of bullshit genres (bullshit letters get found out), it explains the reference letter instead by its multiple interested audiences: the writer must satisfy the student, the admissions committee, and her own conscience at once, and only the right dose of bullshit accomplishes that.

The chapter indicts an expanding class of 'performative bullshit': the video-store service pledge and the UBC mission statement, where a commitment is treated as fulfilled in the very act of being made, so no complaint can even be lodged. George W. Bush's fabricated WMD case for the Iraq war shows the political version - an argument counts as good simply because it was offered as the reason, and when the intelligence proved false another reason was fabricated. In such a world sincerity, irony, and even cynicism become impossible, since only pseudo-motives remain, lacking even sincere self-interest.

chapters.file: ch47 - Chapter 7 - The Importance of Being Earnest A Pragmatic Approach to Bullshitting.md
chapters.relation: Closing the essay, this section argues the bullshit world is inherently stable rather than unstable: the administrator whose whole professional being is appending mission-talk to whatever the university already does is its emblem. The one live remedy is the Jon Stewart gambit - The Daily Show's openly fake news outperforming 'serious' sources, showing by self-consciously flouting the conventions of truth-telling what those conventions were for - and beyond that, actually taking a mission statement seriously enough to rethink higher education's values rather than settle, undeserving, for bullshit.

De Waal's opening salvo: Frankfurt analyzed the concept of bullshit by ordinary language, but the interesting question is the intention with which bullshitting is produced. He announces a contrast between bullshitting and genuine inquiry, and blames bullshit's prevalence partly on a lost confidence that figuring out how things really are is possible or worthwhile.

Building on G.A. Cohen's split of bullshit thinking into a structuralist school (bullshit is an intrinsic feature of products, e.g. texts unclarifiably unclear whatever the author intended) and an intentionalist school (Frankfurt: bullshit is the act done with indifference to truth), the chapter defends intentionalism against the 'insight problem'. The sham astrologer whose Tarot-based celebrity-death prediction happens to come true, and Perry's undergraduates who aced an exam they bullshitted, show that a claim stays bullshit until someone not bullshitting has affirmed it and thereby transformed it into knowledge - just as one person's trash is another's treasure without the chair itself changing.

Against the bullshitter the chapter recruits Peirce: genuine inquiry is defined not by method or results but by the attitude of truly wanting true answers, so homicide detectives, philologists, and car mechanics all count as scientists in this sense. Bullshitting is a free-rider riding the bus of real inquiry - even the bullshitter wants his doctor not to bullshit - and the chapter formulates an epistemic imperative: proceed on the hope that there is a true answer and act from the desire to find it, with fallibilism, not skepticism, the viable stance (the passenger who can occupy any vacant seat cannot occupy them all).

Violations of the epistemic imperative are sorted into Peirce's 'sham reasoning' (the creationist who reasons only to prop up a fixed conclusion), Haack's 'fake reasoning' (corporate-funded research, vote-seeking politicians, the temporary-insanity plea), and the skeptic's premature 'we'll never know' - none of which is bullshitting, which is precisely not caring about truth, like the sales clerk praising shoes at random. Even philosophy can slide into bullshitting when, per Rorty, it becomes 'carrying on the conversation' with truth as what your peers let you get away with; and brainstorming differs from a bull session because brainstormers actually want to discover something.

chapters.file: ch52 - II - The Bull by the Horns.md
chapters.relation: Why do people bullshit? Because liberal democracy, heir to the Cartesian rejection of authority and the Enlightenment's think-for-yourself ideal, expects instant opinions on everything from people detached enough that nothing they say makes a difference; and because a failed search for certainty breeds prophylactic pessimism about inquiry itself. The cure is earnestness - scientists take colleagues' results on trust - though the chapter concedes defensible cases: the formulaic 'It's nice to see you!' as fake reasoning for civility, and friends horsing around for fun.

chapters.file: ch54 - 1 Without the Shit of the Bull.md

chapters.relation: Cohen's autobiographical preface: his youthful struggle with Althusserian French Marxism of the 1960s - interpellation, contradiction and overdetermination - taught him that writings attracting reverent attention can still be bullshit, a lesson sealed when his Marxist discussion group took the name Non-Bullshit Marxism Group, 'Marxism without the shit of the bull'. He also diagnoses the psychology (cognitive dissonance reduction plus adaptive preference formation) by which readers of rebarbative texts overvalue the banal sense they finally extract.

Via the OED's two entries, the chapter finds that 'bullshit' denotes two different things: nonsense or rubbish (output-centered - the shit wears the trousers) and insincere talk (producer-centered - the bull wears the trousers, Frankfurt's kind). Frankfurt's fault is not error but generality: he cast his account of one flower as the 'essence' of the whole garden, ignoring the academically more significant kind that is defined without any reference to a producer's state of mind.

Cohen's main critique: Frankfurt identifies the liar by his goal (misleading about reality) but the bullshitter only at the level of tactic (indifference to the truth of what he says), leaving the bullshitter no distinctive goal - so advertisers and politicians, Frankfurt's own paradigm bullshitters, actually pursue the liar's goal and their bullshitting and lying coincide. Freud's favorite Pinsk/Minsk joke shows tactic and goal can come apart (deceiving by telling the truth), and the Fourth of July orator, contra Frankfurt, might care very much that the audience believe things about the Founding Fathers.

chapters.file: ch58 - 5 Bullshit as Product and Bullshit as Process.md
chapters.relation: Cohen's positive account: bullshit is a feature of texts, paradigmatically 'unclarifiable unclarity' - discourse that cannot be rendered clear without ceasing to be a version of what was said, which is why the way to defend Hegel or Heidegger is to show their texts make sense, not that they cared about truth. A sufficient test is the negation sign: if adding or subtracting it makes no difference to plausibility, as with Sokal's hoax physics, the text is bullshit - though suggestively valuable poetry is spared. 'Bullshitter' then splits into a dispositional reading and an aim reading, only the latter of which always bullshits when producing bullshit.

chapters.file: ch59 - Chapter 9 - The Unity of Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: Cohen concludes that because bullshit can be emitted innocently - even by honest acolytes - the Sokal-style struggle against academic bullshit must target the visible product rather than the producer's hidden intentions, lest innocent traffickers be slandered as insincere or deliberately obscure. Fun as it is to write 'bullshit' over and over in an academic article, the bullshitter/bullshit distinction matters because the justice of the polemic depends on it.

chapters.file: ch60 - No Bullshit, Please, We’re Austrian.md
chapters.relation: Hardcastle proposes to settle the Frankfurt-Cohen quarrel by adding logical positivism to the mix: the Vienna Circle's war on metaphysics was the 1920s-30s' great anti-bullshit program, and both Frankfurt's negligence-of-truth and Cohen's unclarifiable unclarity have precedents in it. Laura Penny's Your Call Is Important to Us supplies the moral heat ('when you fuck with English, you are money-changing in my temple'), while the summary of both positions - the liar needs the truth, the bullshitter does not give a hoot - sets up the Carnap chapters.

chapters.file: ch61 - A Little Carnap in Everyone.md
chapters.relation: Carnap's 'Overcoming Metaphysics through Logical Analysis of Language' supplies the unification: his verificationism renders the invented word 'teavy' meaningless for the same reason Cohen's texts are unclarifiably unclear, while Heidegger's 'The nothing noths' exemplifies the pseudo-sentence whose utterance expresses disregard for meaning - Frankfurt-style bullshitting. The 'toovy' example drives the point home: once a term's synonymy with 'quadrangular' is fixed, professing a further hidden meaning reveals a speaker who never intended to convey information at all.

Meaning, for Carnap, is bearing the right deductive relations to other claims - exactly Cohen's insight that clarity is relational, so that 'clarifying' an unclarifiable text mangles it into something unrecognizable. Carnap's diagnosis of why metaphysics flourishes - metaphysicians express a general attitude toward life (Lebenseinstellung), better expressed through art, and mistake it for a state of affairs - explains bullshit's ubiquity and tolerance; but the metaphysician who knows he says nothing, like Heidegger after Carnap called him on it, is Frankfurt's bullshitter pure and simple.

chapters.file: ch63 - Chapter 10 - Raising the Tone Definition, Bullshit, and the Definition of Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: The unification: Frankfurt's intentionalist bull and Cohen's structuralist shit are two sides of one thing, since a language amenable to misuse meets the bullshitter's ends halfway. The response is gun control for language - not Carnap's ideal language, but shared responsibility for English in our presence, from writing letters to casting votes - ending with Otto Neurath's anti-pseudorationalist insistence that the world's shape reflects our own choices rather than reasons beyond our control: it really is up to us.

chapters.file: ch65 - A Caricature History of Semantics.md
chapters.relation: The chapter christens Frankfurt's innovation 'semantic negligence' on the legal model: the deceptive bullshitter has a duty of care to truth and breaches it without intending the resulting deception, which is why lying (intentional) is more culpable, yet bullshit more insidious because it degrades the commitment to truth on which public discourse depends. Terry Pratchett's characters who applaud 'any man who can tell an outrageous whopper with a gleam in his eye' mark the complicit bull session - bullshit deceives only when it escapes the session and masquerades as ordinary assertion.

A caricature history of semantics centered on Frege's threefold distinction of sense, reference, and tone (Faerbung): 'the evening star' and 'the morning star' share a reference but differ in sense, and 'and' versus 'but' share logical form while differing in tone, which formal logic must suppress. The chapter ends by deploying Stevenson's persuasive definition against the Thouless-style Orwellian fantasy of purging tone-laden words like 'freedom' and 'democratic' from political language: the real remedy is taking tone seriously, since tone does real work in ordinary argument.

Stevenson's persuasive definition - changing a term's descriptive meaning while keeping its emotive force - is restated in Fregean terms as changing sense or reference while representing tone as fixed, yielding a sixteen-fold table of definitional moves (PD, PQD, and beyond). Semantic negligence then grades PDs: the aphoristic 'Conservatism is true socialism' deceives no one, but the definer who hides an argument inside a definition gains rhetorical advantage while risking that his audience endorses conclusions they were never given a fair chance to appraise - analogous to bullshit rather than lying.

Low and high redefinition - widening or narrowing a term's reference - are defined and illustrated by the convicted drunk driver who recasts himself as someone who merely 'had a miscalculated drink', a self-serving move aimed at dodging the pejorative tone of 'drunk driver'. The move partially overlaps persuasive definition (each is a high redefinition of the other's complement) and typically rests on wilful blindness to conventional usage.

Flew's No-True-Scotsman Move - retreating from 'No Scotsman takes sugar with his porridge' to 'No true Scotsman...' when Hamish MacTavish of Inverness falsifies it - is analyzed as a redefinition that converts a bold, falsifiable claim into a vacuous necessary truth. Because the two statements look and sound alike, confusing them (from carelessness as easily as deceit) is semantic negligence, and pressing on as if the original claim still stood is classic Frankfurt bullshit.

Euphemism - the Furies as the 'Kindly Ones', 'sex workers', 'superprompt critical power excursion' for nuclear meltdown - resets a term's tone while preserving its sense and reference, but Germaine Greer's 'euphemism treadmill' shows the pejorative tone rapidly migrates onto each replacement unless underlying attitudes change. The comparative stability of 'gay' and 'black' marks real progress, while most politically correct and nukespeak coinages simply backfire as Greer describes.

The definitional taxonomy at work: MacKinnon and Dworkin's Model Law defines pornography as 'the sexually explicit subordination of women', but backfires in Canadian law into raids on gay bookshops while mainstream pornography survives - reference drift from an intended sense-only change. The three theories of rape (traditional property crime, liberal sex-without-consent, radical feminist 'terrorist institution' of male subordination) show definitions track theories and must be argued for, with the radical redefinition risking a tone-dilution that would 'trivialize legitimate rape'.

chapters.file: ch76 - Is Frankfurt’s Definition of ‘Bullshit’ Itself PD.md
chapters.relation: How backfire is avoided: definitions that stipulate meaning are disguised arguments, legitimate only when the concealed argument is made explicit to all parties and actually won - as with the hard-won consensus definition of 'planet' and the liberal definition of rape. The chapter dismisses essence-based 'real definition' talk, from Plato and Aristotle through the logic-textbook rules, as metaphysically discredited, and proposes 'semantic diligence' in its place.

chapters.file: ch77 - Chapter 11 - Different Kinds and Aspects of Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: Closing chapter 10's circle: Frankfurt's definition of 'bullshit' is itself a persuasive definition of case d - it changes the term's sense and reference while keeping the pejorative tone, as the well-meant 'Help is on its way' to the critically injured shows. Because Frankfurt argues explicitly for his departures from conventional usage, his definition is semantically diligent rather than negligent, though Cohen's complaint that it omits academic bullshit remains to be answered - with which Chapter 11 opens.

Maes and Schaubroeck open on the bookstore irony: Frankfurt's slim bestseller On Bullshit shelved beside Chakra Balancing Kit, The Hidden Messages in Water Crystals, and Astrology: A Cosmic Science - almost as if placed there to illustrate the very bullshit Frankfurt diagnosed as the most salient feature of our culture. They then introduce Cohen's admiring complaint that Frankfurt examined 'just one flower in the lush garden of bullshit', teeing up the academic kind Cohen will define.

chapters.file: ch79 - A Different Take on Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: A faithful reconstruction of Frankfurt: the bullshitter is a slovenly craftsman whose laxity concerns truth rather than detail - spin doctors control every tiny thing except whether what they say is true. The bull session shows indifference alone is not enough, since bullshit adds the pretence that hides that indifference (the Fourth of July orator misrepresents his own state of mind, not American history), whence Frankfurt's conclusion that bullshit is the greater enemy of truth - and the announcement that all three claims (unconcern, concealment, blameworthiness) will be contested.

chapters.file: ch80 - A Different Kind of Bullshit.md
chapters.relation: The Pascal anecdote returns to undermine Frankfurt: Wittgenstein's disgust at 'I feel just like a dog that has been run over' involves no fakery, so pretence is not an essential ingredient of bullshit - mere indifference to truth suffices, as the hypothetical politician who openly stops caring would show. Bullshit emerges as often benign: Ishiguro's butler Stevens in The Remains of the Day comes to see bantering as 'the key to human warmth', Nagel's polite 'How nice to see you!' is convention-governed and no deception, and Wilde's epigrams - nearly all bullshit - explain why our attitude toward bullshit is softer than toward lying.

chapters.file: ch81 - III - It’s All Around Us.md
chapters.relation: Cohen's product-based kind (unclarifiable unclarity, probed by the negation-sign test) is summarized, and the chapter asks whether Frankfurt-bullshit and Cohen-bullshit exhaust the lush garden. They do not: pseudoscience like astrology, chakra balancing, and bogus healing is a third, damaging kind - its practitioners sincerely believe (failing Frankfurt's indifference test) and predict specifically and clearly (failing Cohen's unclarity test) - so insensitivity to evidence and fallacious reasoning must be central to its analysis, better to be vaguely right than precisely wrong.

chapters.file: ch82 - Chapter 12 - The Republic of Bullshit On the Dumbing-Up of Democracy.md
ch83 - Bullshitting and Lying in Politics.md
chapters.relation: Opening Mark Evans's Chapter 12: Frankfurt's claim that democracy especially breeds bullshit, since it charges every citizen with having opinions about everything - the 'Frankfurt thesis' that citizens do not care about truth. It is contrasted with the 'cynicism thesis' (citizens do not care about politics, out of well-founded disillusion with a system that fails to deliver), and both are framed by the objection as old as Plato that political understanding is an expertise we cannot all share - theses argued about, not against, democracy.

holes.name: Performative Utterances (speech acts)
holes.what: Speech acts (promises, pledges, commitments) in which saying the words itself performs the act, with distinct conditions for issuance and fulfillment.
holes.why: Chapter 46's key coinage 'performative bullshit' - commitments treated as fulfilled by their very issuance (video-store pledges, university mission statements) - presupposes exactly this speech-act machinery.

holes.name: J.L. Austin
holes.what: Ordinary-language philosopher who founded speech-act theory with the notion of performative utterances in How to Do Things with Words.
holes.why: Chapter 46 analyzes institutional 'performative bullshit' in explicitly performative terms - commitments issued versus fulfilled - whose framework Austin introduced.

holes.name: G.A. Cohen
holes.what: Marxist political philosopher whose essay 'Deeper into Bullshit' distinguishes product-based (structuralist) bullshit from Frankfurt's intention-based account and coins 'unclarifiable unclarity'.
holes.why: Chapters 48-63 and 77-81 of this unit are organized around Cohen's structuralist/intentionalist split, his OED-based two species, and his critique of Frankfurt's tactic/goal confusion.

holes.name: Louis Althusser
holes.what: Structuralist Marxist theorist of ideological state apparatuses, interpellation, and overdetermination, whose 1960s French school exemplified academic obscurity for Cohen.
holes.why: Chapter 55 names the Althusserian school and its concepts of interpellation and overdetermination as the paradigm case of the academic bullshit Cohen became least tolerant of.

holes.name: Rudolf Carnap
holes.what: Logical positivist whose 'Overcoming Metaphysics through the Logical Analysis of Language' diagnosed metaphysics as meaningless pseudo-sentences, targeting Heidegger's 'The nothing noths'.
holes.why: Chapters 61-63 build the unification of Frankfurt's and Cohen's bullshit directly on Carnap's teavy/toovy examples, his notion of pseudo-statements, and his diagnosis of metaphysics as disguised expression of a life-attitude.

holes.name: Verificationism (the verifiability theory of meaning)
holes.what: The logical-positivist doctrine that a statement is meaningful only if it can be verified or deduced from other meaningful statements, rendering metaphysical and theological utterances pseudo-statements.
holes.why: Chapter 61 uses Carnap's verificationist test on 'teavy' and 'The nothing noths' as the precise forerunner of Cohen's unclarifiable-unclarity bullshit test.

holes.name: Charles L. Stevenson
holes.what: American emotivist ethicist who coined 'persuasive definition' - redefining a term's descriptive meaning while preserving its emotive force - in Ethics and Language.
holes.why: Chapters 66-67 and 75-77 build their entire analysis of definitional bullshit, semantic negligence, and backfire on Stevenson's PD/PQD machinery.

holes.name: Persuasive Definition
holes.what: A redefinition that changes a term's descriptive meaning (sense or reference) while covertly preserving its emotive force (tone), thereby smuggling in an argument as a definition.
holes.why: Chapters 66-77 analyze drunk-driver excuses, the No-True-Scotsman move, euphemism, the pornography and rape definitions, and even Frankfurt's own definition of 'bullshit' as instances of PD and its backfire.

holes.name: No True Scotsman Move
holes.what: The ad hoc rescue move (named by Antony Flew) of redefining a group term to exclude counterexamples, converting a falsifiable generalization into a vacuous necessary truth.
holes.why: Chapter 70's core example - Hamish MacTavish and his sugared porridge - is analyzed as high/low redefinition plus semantic negligence ending in Frankfurt-style bullshit.

holes.name: The Euphemism Treadmill
holes.what: The process, observed by Germaine Greer, by which euphemisms acquire the pejorative tone of the terms they replace and must be endlessly substituted for themselves.
holes.why: Chapter 74's whole argument is that tone-resetting euphemisms (from 'Eumenides' to politically correct and nukespeak coinages) backfire via this treadmill unless underlying attitudes genuinely change.

holes.name: The Demarcation Problem (pseudoscience)
holes.what: The problem of distinguishing science from pseudoscience by criteria beyond the sincerity or clarity of its practitioners, such as sensitivity to evidence.
holes.why: Chapter 81 argues astrology, chakra healing, and numerology are a third kind of bullshit - sincere and clear but evidence-insensitive - requiring exactly the demarcation account neither Frankfurt nor Cohen supplies.
